title: Grammarly Review 2026: Is the AI Writing Assistant Still Worth $12/Month?
content:
*Affiliate disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This never affects our ratings or recommendations. [Full disclosure](/disclosure)*

*Last updated: July 5, 2026*

## Quick Answer

**Grammarly** is the industry-leading AI writing assistant trusted by over 40 million people and 50,000 organizations worldwide. In 2026, Grammarly has evolved far beyond simple spell-checking — it's now a comprehensive AI-powered communication platform that includes AI agents (Paraphraser, Proofreader, Reader Reactions), multilingual support in 25+ languages, AI text detection and humanization, and enterprise-grade security features. The **Pro plan at $12/month (billed annually)** delivers the best value for most individual users, unlocking full-sentence rewrites, tone adjustment, plagiarism detection, citation generation, and 2,000 AI prompts per month. For teams and organizations, the Enterprise plan through Superhuman Go offers unlimited AI prompts, custom style guides, brand tones, and advanced security controls. While the free version is genuinely useful for basic grammar, the Pro plan is what transforms Grammarly from a simple proofreading tool into your always-on AI writing partner.

| **Customer Support** | 7.8/10 | Good for paid users, limited for free tier |
| **Overall Score** | **93/100** | The best AI writing assistant in 2026 |

## Pros and Cons

### Pros

- **Unmatched grammar accuracy** — Corrects complex grammatical errors that competitors miss, including subject-verb agreement, misplaced modifiers, and tense consistency across all English variants (US, UK, AU, CA)
- **Powerful AI agents** — The Paraphraser, Proofreader, and Reader Reactions agents go beyond basic grammar checking to help you refine tone, anticipate how readers will perceive your message, and polish your writing
- **Works everywhere** — Browser extensions (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge), desktop apps (Windows, Mac), mobile (iOS, Android), and direct integration with Google Docs, Microsoft Word, Outlook, Slack, LinkedIn, and 500,000+ websites and apps
- **Multilingual writing support** — Real-time grammar and clarity suggestions in 25+ languages with advanced tone detection in 6 languages (English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian)
- **AI text detection built in** — Grammarly's Authorship feature identifies AI-generated text and the Humanizer agent helps make it sound more natural, a unique combination in the market
- **Enterprise-grade security** — SOC 2 Type 2 certified, GDPR compliant, BYOK encryption, DLP, SAML SSO, and SCIM provisioning for organizations
- **Generous free tier** — The free version offers genuine value with spelling, grammar, basic tone detection, and 100 AI prompts per month — no credit card required
- **Citation and plagiarism combo** — Automatic citation generation (APA, MLA, Chicago) combined with plagiarism checking against 16 billion web pages makes it essential for students and researchers

### Cons

- **Premium pricing** — At $30/month for monthly billing, Pro is significantly more expensive than ProWritingAid ($120/year) and LanguageTool ($79/year). Annual commitment is almost mandatory for reasonable pricing
- **No offline mode for desktop** — The desktop app requires an internet connection. If you're writing on a plane or in a low-connectivity area, Grammarly's features are unavailable
- **Privacy concerns for free users** — The free tier processes all text through Grammarly's servers. While the company states it does not sell data, privacy-conscious users may prefer local-only alternatives like LanguageTool's desktop app
- **Billing practices draw complaints** — Trustpilot reviews (2.1/5 rating) frequently cite automatic renewal charges without clear reminders and difficulty canceling subscriptions. Grammarly has improved its cancellation flow in 2026, but the damage to reputation persists
- **Limited AI prompt allowance on Pro** — 2,000 AI prompts per month on the Pro plan sounds generous but heavy users who rely on Grammarly for daily content generation may hit the limit quickly
- **No PDF or image support** — Unlike some competitors, Grammarly cannot analyze text in PDFs or images — you need to copy-paste the text manually

## Who Is Grammarly For?

Grammarly delivers different value depending on your use case. Here's who benefits most — and who should look elsewhere.

### ✅ Grammarly Is Ideal For

- **Professionals and knowledge workers** who write emails, reports, proposals, and Slack messages daily. Grammarly works inside every tool you already use — no copying and pasting required. The tone detector ensures your messages land with the right intention every time
- **Students and academics** who need citation generation (APA, MLA, Chicago), plagiarism detection against 16 billion web pages and ProQuest databases, and clarity suggestions for complex arguments
- **Content creators and marketers** who produce high volumes of blog posts, social media content, newsletters, and ad copy. The Paraphraser AI agent and tone adjustment features help maintain consistency across channels
- **Non-native English speakers** who want to write with native-level fluency. Grammarly's fluency suggestions are industry-leading, helping catch unnatural phrasing, word choice issues, and sentence structure problems that basic grammar checkers miss
- **Enterprise teams** that need consistent brand voice, style guides, and analytics on team writing quality. The Effective Communication Score and Analytics Dashboard provide actionable insights for team leads
- **Job seekers** who need polished resumes and cover letters. Grammarly's Resume Builder AI agent helps structure and optimize resumes for ATS systems and human readers alike

### ❌ Grammarly Is Not Ideal For

- **Budget-conscious writers** who can get 80% of the functionality from ProWritingAid at half the annual price. If you're primarily writing creative fiction or long-form content and don't need browser-wide integration, ProWritingAid offers better value
- **Writers who primarily work offline** — if you frequently write in environments without internet access (flights, remote locations, secure facilities), Grammarly's cloud dependency is a dealbreaker
- **Users who need PDF or image text checking** — Grammarly only works with editable text. For PDF proofreading, you'll need to copy-paste content or use a different tool entirely
- **Casual writers who only need basic spell-check** — the free built-in spell checkers in Google Docs, Microsoft Word, and Apple Pages are sufficient for basic needs. Grammarly's premium features only justify themselves with regular, high-stakes writing

## Detailed Features Breakdown

### AI Agents: The New Frontier of Writing Assistance

Grammarly's most significant evolution in 2025-2026 has been the introduction of specialized AI agents — purpose-built tools that go beyond grammar checking to address specific writing challenges.

**The Paraphraser** lets you fine-tune your voice without losing your ideas. Need to make an email sound more professional? Rewrite a blog paragraph to be more engaging? The Paraphraser adjusts tone, formality, and clarity while preserving your original intent. Unlike competitors' basic rewording tools, Grammarly's Paraphraser understands context — a technical document gets different treatment than a marketing email.

**The Proofreader** is Grammarly's next-generation version of its classic grammar engine. It catches everything from basic typos to complex structural issues like dangling modifiers, inconsistent verb tenses across paragraphs, and subject-verb agreement in long sentences. The 2026 version has improved accuracy by roughly 15% compared to 2024, particularly for complex sentence structures.

**Reader Reactions** is perhaps Grammarly's most innovative AI agent. Before sending an important email or publishing a blog post, you can set a target reader persona (manager, client, colleague, professor) and see how they're likely to react — confused, impressed, persuaded, or skeptical. This pre-emptive feedback loop helps you adjust tone and clarity before it's too late.

**The AI Detector** and **Humanizer** form a complementary pair. The Detector identifies passages that read as AI-generated, which is increasingly important for academic integrity and brand authenticity. The Humanizer then helps you rephrase AI-generated text to sound more natural and personal — a unique feature that acknowledges how much writing now starts with AI assistance.

**The Citation Finder** automatically identifies claims in your text that need citations and suggests sources, formatting them in APA, MLA, or Chicago style. This is particularly useful for students and researchers who often discover missing citations during final review.

### Tone Detection and Writing Goals

Grammarly's tone detector is the most nuanced in the industry. It doesn't just tell you your text sounds "formal" or "informal" — it identifies specific tonal dimensions including confident, friendly, diplomatic, direct, enthusiastic, and urgent. This granularity matters when you're sending sensitive communications: a Slack message to your boss about a project delay needs a different tone than a celebration announcement to the whole team.

The Writing Goals feature lets you set intentions before you start writing: audience (general, knowledgeable, expert), formality (informal, neutral, formal), domain (academic, business, casual, creative, technical), and intent (inform, describe, convince, tell a story). Grammarly then tailors all its suggestions to match these goals — if you're writing a technical whitepaper for expert readers, it won't flag jargon as a clarity issue.

### Multilingual Support: Beyond English

Grammarly's 2026 multilingual expansion is a game-changer for international users. The platform now supports real-time writing suggestions in 25+ languages including Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and more. The paid plans offer advanced features (clarity, tone, fluency) in 6 core languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, and Italian.

The in-line translation feature is particularly practical — highlight any text in 19 supported languages and get an instant translation without leaving your document. This is invaluable for teams working across time zones and language barriers.

### Enterprise Features: Brand Consistency at Scale

For organizations, Grammarly's Enterprise plan (available through Superhuman Go) offers capabilities that individual plans simply can't match.

**Style Guides** let you codify your brand's writing rules — preferred terminology, capitalization conventions, tone guidelines, and formatting preferences. Once configured, every team member receives real-time suggestions that align with your brand voice, whether they're writing marketing copy, support tickets, or internal memos.

**Brand Tones** ensure every communication sounds like your company. Define up to unlimited brand tones (friendly and approachable for marketing, direct and authoritative for legal, warm and empathetic for support) and Grammarly enforces them automatically.

**Snippets** are reusable text blocks that teams can insert with keyboard shortcuts — perfect for standard email responses, legal disclaimers, onboarding messages, and any text that gets written repeatedly.

The **Analytics Dashboard** provides team leads with visibility into writing quality across the organization. The Effective Communication Score quantifies how clear, engaging, and correct your team's writing is, while the ROI Report connects writing improvement to business outcomes.

**Security features** include BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) encryption, Data Loss Prevention (DLP), SAML-based Single Sign-On, SCIM provisioning for automated user management, audit logs via API, session timeout controls, and confidential mode for sensitive documents.

## Pricing

Grammarly offers four distinct plans designed for different user profiles. Here's what each plan includes and — importantly — what it doesn't.

| Plan | Monthly | Annual (per month) | Best For |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Free** | $0 | $0 | Casual writers, students trying it out |
| **Pro** | $30/mo | $12/mo ($144/year) | Professionals, freelancers, serious students |
| **Business** | $40/user/mo | $33/user/mo ($396/user/year) | Teams of 3+, agencies, SMBs |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Custom (Contact Sales) | Large organizations, universities |

### Hidden Costs You Should Know About

Grammarly's pricing is transparent on the surface, but there are nuances worth understanding before subscribing:

- **Auto-renewal at full price**: Grammarly subscriptions auto-renew at the standard rate. If you signed up during a promotion (common discounts: 40-60% off annual Pro), your renewal will be at the full $144/year. Set a calendar reminder before your renewal date
- **No mid-plan refunds**: Grammarly does not offer pro-rated refunds if you cancel mid-cycle. If you cancel an annual plan after 3 months, you lose access immediately (no refund for remaining 9 months)
- **Business plan minimum**: While Grammarly advertises "teams of 3+", the Business plan shows the best value for teams of 5+ where style guides and brand tones become genuinely useful
- **Enterprise pricing is opaque**: No pricing is published for Enterprise. Expect to negotiate based on seat count, with volume discounts starting around 50+ users
- **AI prompt overages**: On the Pro plan, hitting your 2,000 AI prompts/month limit doesn't trigger an upsell — it simply stops working. Heavy AI users should consider Enterprise (unlimited prompts) or supplement with another AI tool

### Breakeven Analysis: Is Pro Worth It?

At $144/year, Grammarly Pro costs $0.39/day. If you write professionally and Grammarly saves you even 5 minutes per day in proofreading, rewriting, and tone adjustment, that's 30 hours per year — a return of roughly $4.80 per dollar spent at minimum wage. For knowledge workers billing $50-150/hour, the ROI is 10-30x.

The question isn't really "can I afford Grammarly Pro?" — it's "can I afford the mistakes Grammarly would catch?"

## Buyer's Guide: How to Choose the Right AI Writing Assistant

Choosing an AI writing assistant in 2026 isn't just about finding the best grammar checker — it's about finding the tool that fits your workflow, your writing goals, and your budget. Here's what to prioritize:

**1. Integration depth matters more than feature count.** A writing assistant with 100 features that only works on one platform is less useful than a tool with 50 features that works everywhere you write. Grammarly's 500,000+ integrations are its biggest practical advantage — you don't have to change your workflow to use it.

**2. AI writing features are the new battleground.** In 2024, grammar checking was the differentiator. In 2026, it's AI agents. Tools like Grammarly's Reader Reactions and Paraphraser, ProWritingAid's Rephrase, and Wordtune's Spices represent the next generation of writing assistance. If you're choosing today, prioritize tools with active AI development.

**3. Budget vs. value: the annual commitment trap.** Every writing tool offers steep discounts for annual billing. Before committing, use the free tier for at least 2 weeks to ensure the tool fits your workflow. A $144/year subscription you don't use is infinitely more expensive than a $30 monthly plan you cancel after one month.

**4. Privacy requirements dictate your options.** If you work with confidential documents (legal contracts, medical records, financial data), you need a tool that offers local processing or enterprise-grade encryption. Grammarly's Enterprise plan with BYOK is suitable for regulated industries. LanguageTool offers a self-hosted option for maximum privacy.

**5. Non-native English support is not equal across tools.** Grammarly's fluency suggestions are specifically designed for non-native speakers and catch errors that native-oriented checkers miss. If English is your second language, Grammarly's advantage in this area alone may justify the premium.

## Competitor Comparisons

### Grammarly vs. ProWritingAid

ProWritingAid is Grammarly's strongest competitor for long-form writers and authors. At $120/year, it's about 17% cheaper than Grammarly Pro. ProWritingAid excels at in-depth writing reports — it provides over 20 different analyses including pacing, dialogue tags, sentence length variety, and readability scores that are invaluable for novelists and content writers producing 5,000+ word pieces.

However, ProWritingAid's integrations are significantly narrower. It works as a browser extension, desktop app, and Microsoft Word add-in, but doesn't integrate with Google Docs, Slack, or LinkedIn. Its tone detection is rudimentary compared to Grammarly's, and it lacks AI agents like Reader Reactions and the Humanizer. Grammarly's real-time suggestions are also noticeably faster — ProWritingAid's more thorough analysis comes with a 1-3 second delay that interrupts writing flow.

**Winner for most users: Grammarly Pro** — better integrations, faster suggestions, and AI agents make it worth the $24/year premium. Choose ProWritingAid if you're primarily a creative writer who values deep style analysis over real-time assistance.

### Grammarly vs. Hemingway Editor

Hemingway Editor takes the opposite approach — instead of adding AI assistance, it strips writing down to its essentials. The desktop app ($19.99 one-time purchase) highlights complex sentences, passive voice, adverbs, and readability issues. It's beloved by bloggers and journalists who want to write with simplicity and punch.

But Hemingway is not a grammar checker. It won't catch subject-verb agreement errors, spelling mistakes, or punctuation issues. It has no AI features at all — no paraphrasing, no tone detection, no citation generation. It's a complementary tool, not a competitor. Many professional writers use Hemingway alongside Grammarly: Hemingway for initial editing (cut the fluff) and Grammarly for final polish (catch the errors).

**Winner: Different tools.** Use both if you can — Hemingway for clarity first, Grammarly for correctness second.

### Grammarly vs. QuillBot

QuillBot started as a paraphrasing tool and has expanded into a full writing suite with grammar checking, plagiarism detection, citation generation, and a summarizer. At $99.95/year for Premium, it's about 31% cheaper than Grammarly Pro.

QuillBot's paraphraser is excellent — its 7 modes (Standard, Fluency, Formal, Simple, Creative, Expand, Shorten) offer fine-grained control that Grammarly's Paraphraser agent doesn't quite match. The Summarizer is a genuinely useful addition for research-heavy writing.

But QuillBot's grammar checker is noticeably less accurate than Grammarly's, particularly for complex sentences and nuanced tone issues. Its integrations are limited to Chrome, Word, and a web editor — no desktop app, no mobile keyboard, no Google Docs integration. For most users, QuillBot is a strong secondary tool for paraphrasing, not a Grammarly replacement.

**Winner for grammar and integrations: Grammarly Pro.** Winner for paraphrasing versatility at a lower price: QuillBot.

### Grammarly vs. LanguageTool

LanguageTool is the leading open-source alternative, with a Premium plan at approximately $79/year — roughly 55% of Grammarly Pro's price. It supports 30+ languages (more than Grammarly) and offers a self-hosted option for privacy-conscious organizations.

LanguageTool picks up many of the same errors as Grammarly, particularly for European languages where it often outperforms Grammarly. However, its English grammar checking is noticeably less sophisticated — it misses nuanced tone issues, word choice problems, and stylistic inconsistencies that Grammarly catches consistently.

For organizations that need grammar checking across many languages with strong privacy controls, LanguageTool is compelling. For English-first writers who want the best possible suggestions, Grammarly remains superior.

**Winner for English writing: Grammarly Pro.** Winner for multilingual + privacy: LanguageTool.

### Grammarly vs. Wordtune

Wordtune, now part of the AI21 Labs ecosystem, focuses on rewriting and tone adjustment rather than grammar checking. Its "Spices" feature adds facts, examples, counterarguments, and jokes to your writing — a unique capability that no other tool offers.

Wordtune's rewrite suggestions are excellent for creative and marketing copy, often producing more varied and interesting alternatives than Grammarly. But Wordtune doesn't check grammar, doesn't detect plagiarism, doesn't generate citations, and has limited integrations.

**Winner: Different use cases.** Use Grammarly for correctness and professional polish. Use Wordtune for creative rewriting when you need fresh angles on existing text.

## Real-World Performance and User Feedback

Grammarly's massive user base — 40 million individual users and 50,000 organizations — generates a wealth of real-world feedback that reveals consistent patterns.

### What Users Consistently Praise

Professional users on G2 (4.5/5, 1,800+ reviews) and Capterra (4.6/5) highlight Grammarly's seamless integration as its biggest strength. Reviews frequently mention that Grammarly "just works" without interrupting workflow — the suggestions appear inline in whatever tool you're using, and accepting them is a single click.

Non-native English speakers provide some of Grammarly's most enthusiastic feedback. On the Apple App Store (4.7/5, 2.6M+ ratings), international users consistently credit Grammarly with improving their professional communication and confidence. One recurring theme: Grammarly catches errors that "sound wrong" to native speakers but are invisible to non-native writers — word choice, register, and cultural context.

The AI agents launched in 2025-2026 have been well-received. The Paraphraser in particular earns praise for preserving meaning while adjusting tone — a common complaint about earlier AI rewriting tools was that they changed what you actually meant to say.

### What Users Consistently Criticize

Trustpilot (2.1/5) reveals the dark side of Grammarly's user experience, though the complaints follow a predictable pattern: billing issues. Users report automatic renewal charges without clear prior notification, difficulty canceling subscriptions, and confusion about refund policies. Grammarly improved its cancellation flow in early 2026 (you can now cancel directly from account settings without contacting support), but the damage to Trustpilot scores persists.

Performance complaints have decreased significantly since 2024. Earlier versions of the browser extension were resource-heavy and could slow down web apps like Google Docs. The 2026 version is noticeably lighter, and Grammarly's switch to more efficient AI models has improved suggestion speed.

The 2,000 AI prompts/month cap on Pro plans generates occasional frustration. Power users who leverage AI heavily for content creation find themselves hitting the limit within 2-3 weeks. Grammarly's position is clear — heavy AI users belong on Enterprise plans — but the gap between Pro limits and Enterprise pricing leaves a segment of users underserved.

### Expert and Industry Recognition

Grammarly has maintained its position as the category-defining product in AI writing assistance. It consistently ranks #1 in independent comparisons from TechRadar, PCMag, and Zapier. The company's SOC 2 Type 2 certification and GDPR compliance make it one of the few AI writing tools that enterprise IT departments approve without hesitation.

The Superhuman acquisition in 2025 has accelerated Grammarly's enterprise capabilities, particularly the Go assistant that works across every application on your computer — a capability that no competitor currently matches.

## 7 Tips to Get the Most Out of Grammarly

**1. Set Writing Goals before every important document.** Take 10 seconds to configure audience, formality, domain, and intent. Grammarly's suggestions become dramatically more relevant when it knows you're writing a formal business proposal rather than a casual team update. The difference in suggestion quality is night and day.

**2. Use the tone detector as a "second read" before sending.** Before hitting send on an important email or Slack message, glance at the tone indicator. If you intended to sound confident but Grammarly detects "uncertain," you know to revise. This 3-second check has saved countless professional relationships.

**3. Create a personal dictionary immediately.** Grammarly flags product names, technical terms, and brand-specific jargon as errors. Add your company name, product names, industry acronyms, and commonly used technical terms to your dictionary to eliminate false positives and reduce alert fatigue.

**4. Use the Pro plan's 7-day free trial strategically.** Don't just test whether Grammarly works — test whether it works within your actual workflow. Write 3-4 real documents during the trial period: an important email, a report, a social media post, and a longer document. If Grammarly doesn't noticeably improve at least 2 of these, the free tier may suffice.

**5. Master the keyboard shortcuts.** Grammarly's interface is designed for mouse use, but keyboard shortcuts exist. Alt+G (Windows) or Option+G (Mac) opens the Grammarly widget. Tab accepts a suggestion. These two shortcuts alone can cut your editing time in half.

**6. Leverage Snippets for repetitive writing (Business/Enterprise).** If your team sends the same types of emails repeatedly — customer onboarding, support follow-ups, meeting recaps — create Snippets. A 2-minute investment in creating a Snippet saves hours of re-typing over a year.

**7. Schedule a quarterly writing review with Analytics (Enterprise).** The Analytics Dashboard isn't just for managers — individual writers can see their Effective Communication Score trends over time. Use this data to identify weak spots (are your emails less clear than your reports? Is your formality inconsistent?) and focus your improvement efforts.

## FAQ

### Is Grammarly really free?

Yes. Grammarly's Free plan is genuinely functional with no time limit and no credit card required. You get real-time spelling and grammar corrections, basic tone detection, and 100 AI prompts per month. However, the most valuable features — full-sentence rewrites, tone adjustment, plagiarism detection, citation generation, and advanced AI agents — require a paid plan.

### How much does Grammarly Pro cost?

Grammarly Pro costs $30/month when billed monthly or $144/year ($12/month) when billed annually. The annual plan saves you 60% compared to monthly billing. A 7-day free trial is available for new Pro subscribers, and promotional discounts of 40-60% off the annual plan are common.

### Is Grammarly Premium the same as Grammarly Pro?

Yes. Grammarly rebranded its Premium plan to "Pro" in 2025 as part of a broader product repositioning. The features and pricing remained the same — only the name changed. If you see references to "Grammarly Premium" in older reviews or articles, they're referring to what is now called Grammarly Pro.

### Does Grammarly work with Google Docs?

Yes. Grammarly integrates directly with Google Docs through its browser extension. Once installed, Grammarly suggestions appear inline as you type in Google Docs, exactly as they do in other supported applications. The integration is one of Grammarly's most-used features.

### Can Grammarly detect AI-generated text?

Yes. Grammarly's AI Detector agent identifies passages that were likely generated by AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini. This feature is available on Pro and Enterprise plans. Grammarly also offers a Humanizer agent that helps you rephrase AI-generated text to sound more natural and personal.

### Is Grammarly safe for confidential documents?

For enterprise users, yes. Grammarly's Enterprise plan includes BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) encryption, Data Loss Prevention (DLP), SOC 2 Type 2 certification, and GDPR compliance. These security features make Grammarly suitable for regulated industries including healthcare, finance, and legal. For free and Pro users, text is processed on Grammarly's servers — the company states it does not sell user data, but privacy-conscious users handling sensitive information should use the Enterprise plan or a local-only alternative.

### Does Grammarly work offline?

No. Grammarly requires an active internet connection for all its features, including the desktop app. The spell-checking, grammar suggestions, tone detection, and AI agents all rely on cloud processing. If you frequently work in environments without internet access, consider LanguageTool's offline desktop app or the built-in spelling and grammar checkers in Microsoft Word and Google Docs.

### What's the difference between Grammarly Business and Enterprise?

Grammarly Business ($33/user/month annual) is designed for small to medium teams and includes Style Guides, Brand Tones, Snippets, Knowledge Share, an Analytics Dashboard, and priority support. Grammarly Enterprise (custom pricing) adds enterprise-grade security features: BYOK encryption, DLP, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, audit logs API, session timeout, confidential mode, and unlimited AI prompts. Enterprise also includes an ROI Report and individual analytics that Business doesn't offer.

### Does Grammarly work in Spanish and other languages?

Yes. Grammarly supports real-time writing suggestions in 25+ languages. The free plan offers basic spelling and grammar checking across all supported languages. The Pro plan adds advanced features (clarity, tone, fluency) in 6 languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, and Italian. Grammarly also includes in-line translation across 19 languages.

### Can I use Grammarly on my phone?

Yes. Grammarly offers dedicated mobile apps for iOS (rated 4.7/5 on the App Store) and Android (rated 4.2/5 on Google Play). The Grammarly Keyboard integrates with all apps on your phone, providing real-time writing suggestions in messages, emails, social media posts, and any text field. The mobile apps sync with your account, so your personal dictionary and preferences carry over.

### Can I cancel Grammarly anytime?

Yes. As of 2026, you can cancel your Grammarly subscription directly from your account settings without contacting customer support. However, Grammarly does not offer pro-rated refunds — if you cancel an annual plan mid-cycle, you retain access until the end of your billing period but won't receive a refund for unused months. The cancellation process is significantly improved from earlier years when it required contacting support.

## Conclusion

Grammarly has earned its position as the world's leading AI writing assistant through relentless execution on two fronts: making writing better and making that help frictionless. The 2026 version — with its AI agents, multilingual support, and enterprise-grade capabilities — is the most capable version yet, and the Superhuman Go integration makes it genuinely ubiquitous across every application you use.

For individual professionals, the **Pro plan at $12/month (annual)** represents excellent value. The daily time saved from automatic proofreading, tone adjustment, and AI-powered rewrites far exceeds the daily cost. The free tier is genuinely useful, but the gap between Free and Pro is substantial — once you've experienced full-sentence rewrites and tone adjustment, it's hard to go back.

For teams, the **Business plan** provides the brand consistency tools that transform Grammarly from an individual productivity tool into an organizational communication asset. Style Guides and Brand Tones ensure every team member sounds like your company.

The biggest criticism of Grammarly — its premium pricing — is valid for budget-conscious users who can find 80% of the functionality elsewhere for less. But if writing quality directly impacts your professional reputation, business outcomes, or academic success, Grammarly Pro is one of the highest-ROI software subscriptions available in 2026.

**Ready to improve your writing?** [Try Grammarly Pro free for 7 days](https://www.grammarly.com/plans) and experience the difference that AI-powered writing assistance makes in your daily communication.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Grammarly integrates directly with Google Docs through its browser extension. Once installed, Grammarly suggestions appear inline as you type in Google Docs, exactly as they do in other supported applications. The integration is one of Grammarly's most-used features.

mainEntity.name: Is Grammarly safe for confidential documents?

acceptedAnswer.text: For enterprise users, yes. Grammarly's Enterprise plan includes BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) encryption, Data Loss Prevention (DLP), SOC 2 Type 2 certification, and GDPR compliance. These security features make Grammarly suitable for regulated industries including healthcare, finance, and legal. For free and Pro users, text is processed on Grammarly's servers — the company states it does not sell user data, but privacy-conscious users handling sensitive information should use the Enterprise plan or a local-only alternative.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Grammarly Business and Enterprise?

acceptedAnswer.text: Grammarly Business ($33/user/month annual) is designed for small to medium teams and includes Style Guides, Brand Tones, Snippets, Knowledge Share, an Analytics Dashboard, and priority support. Grammarly Enterprise (custom pricing) adds enterprise-grade security features: BYOK encryption, DLP, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, audit logs API, session timeout, confidential mode, and unlimited AI prompts. Enterprise also includes an ROI Report and individual analytics that Business doesn't offer.

mainEntity.name: Does Grammarly work in Spanish and other languages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Grammarly supports real-time writing suggestions in 25+ languages. The free plan offers basic spelling and grammar checking across all supported languages. The Pro plan adds advanced features (clarity, tone, fluency) in 6 languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, and Italian. Grammarly also includes in-line translation across 19 languages including Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Dutch.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Grammarly on my phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Grammarly offers dedicated mobile apps for iOS (rated 4.7/5 on the App Store with 2.6M+ ratings) and Android (rated 4.2/5 on Google Play). The Grammarly Keyboard integrates with all apps on your phone, providing real-time writing suggestions in messages, emails, social media posts, and any text field. The mobile apps sync with your account so your personal dictionary and preferences carry over.
